s1.syndrome_frame: oral pain and bleeding with radiographic evidence of bone and tooth resorption
salient_findings: cervical areas of rarefaction on periapical radiographs
radiolucent resorptive lesions on cone-beam computed tomography
key_facts: 55-year-old woman
generalized bleeding on probing
clinical attachment loss
stage II, grade II periodontitis
periapical radiographs showed cervical areas of rarefaction
endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors
5 mm probing depth on palatal aspects of both teeth
cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions
lesions originated from external palatal surface and perforated into pulp space
asymptomatic to percussion and palpation

shortlist.label: External Cervical Resorption
shortlist.why_kept: radiographic evidence of cervical areas of rarefaction and cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions

shortlist.label: Asymptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis
shortlist.why_kept: endodontic evaluation was normal for both central incisors and presence of radiolucent resorptive lesions

shortlist.label: Periodontitis
shortlist.why_kept: generalized bleeding on probing, clinical attachment loss, and stage II, grade II periodontitis

shortlist.label: Internal Cervical Resorption
shortlist.why_kept: possibility of resorptive lesions originating from internal tooth structure

shortlist.label: Pulpal Necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: potential consequence of asymptomatic irreversible pulpitis and external cervical resorption

raw.rationale: Cone-beam computed tomography demonstrated radiolucent resorptive lesions cervically on the palatal aspects of teeth, which is consistent with external cervical resorption.

rejected.label: Asymptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis
rejected.why: Normal endodontic evaluation and lack of symptoms

rejected.label: Periodontitis
rejected.why: While present, it does not explain the specific radiolucent resorptive lesions

rejected.label: Internal Cervical Resorption
rejected.why: Lesions originated from external palatal surface, not internally

rejected.label: Pulpal Necrosis
rejected.why: Normal response to cold testing and lack of symptoms
